lawRefs: Ark. Code § 26-51-201(a)(4) as amended by Act 1 of the First Extraordinary Session of 2026 (HB 1001, approved 2026-05-06)
Ark. Code § 26-51-307 ($6,000 retirement exemption; Social Security exempt)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Brackets are the statutory tax-year-2026 table enacted by Act 1 of the May 2026 special session, which cut the top rate from 3.9% to 3.7% retroactive to 2026-01-01 (Tax Foundation's January 2026 table still shows 3.9%). Arkansas has TWO tables chosen by total net income: the table encoded here applies to net income <= $94,700 (0% to $5,599, 2% to $11,199, 3% to $15,999, 3.4% to $26,399, 3.7% to $94,700). Taxpayers with net income > $94,700 instead use: 2% on $0-$4,700 and 3.7% above, less a bracket adjustment of $290 at $94,701-$94,800 declining $10 per $100 to $0 above $97,600. At high incomes the upper table yields about $290 more tax than the encoded table. Same table for every filing status; married couples may file separately on the same return (each spouse taxed individually), which usually lowers tax. Standard deduction $2,470 per taxpayer ($4,940 MFJ) and $29 personal tax credit per exemption are from the DFA Withholding Tax Formula effective 01/01/2026 (indexed 2026 amounts; Tax Foundation 2026 agrees). Extra $29 credit for age 65+ (or a $29 '65 special' credit if not claiming a retirement exemption) is a credit, not a deduction. Starting point is Arkansas's own gross-income computation (federalAGI used as proxy). Social Security fully exempt. First $6,000 of employer-sponsored pension income is exempt at any age; IRA distributions qualify only after age 59 1/2; one $6,000 total per taxpayer. 50% of net long-term capital gain is exempt (gain above $10 million fully exempt).

flags.brackets: simplified: table for net income <= 94,700; above that a second table (2% to 4,700, then 3.7%, no 0% band) applies with a phase-in adjustment through 97,600
flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: 6,000 at any age for employer pensions; IRA distributions only after 59 1/2; military retirement fully exempt
